items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: that's where I had a chance to first hear Earl Hines at the Apex Club, playing piano with Jimmy Noone.

ctx.x: She went and joined Earl Hines' band. We heard her in Cincinnati, brought her back to St. Louis, had Chester Lane to write You Go To My Head, made several arrangements behind her. We took her downtown to a wholesale house where she could buy four or five little evening dresses. They were cheap. But things were rough back in those days. People weren't wearing $100 dresses back in those days. And this was a wholesale place, and she was -- she got to be a Miss Any. (Unintelligible) She was real popular. People were…
Then she started making a little money on the intermissions.
